title: The Hydrogen Spectrum — Origin & Spectral Series
notes: When hydrogen gas is excited (e.g. electrically), electrons absorb energy and jump to higher tracks; when they fall back down to lower tracks, they release that exact energy as light of a specific wavelength
Because transitions happen only between specific fixed tracks, the emitted light forms discrete, sharp spectral lines rather than a continuous rainbow

Each spectral series corresponds to electrons landing on one specific base track (n₁): **Lyman** → n₁ = 1 (ultraviolet, invisible); **Balmer** → n₁ = 2 (the only series visible to the human eye, as coloured lines); **Paschen** → n₁ = 3 (infrared); **Brackett** → n₁ = 4 (infrared); **Pfund** → n₁ = 5 (far-infrared)
